papers.authors: Guegan JP, Bonhomme B, Peyraud F, Rey C, Cousin S, Aldea M, Barlesi F, Besse B et al.

papers.reason: 为ICI耐药机制（免疫排除）提供区室分辨的分子图谱，可为后续生物标志物开发与联合治疗（如基质靶向+ICB）研究提供假说与候选特征，但当前证据不足以改变临床决策
papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has reshaped the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains limited to a subset of patients. One major pattern of resistance is immune exclusion, in which CD8+ T cells accumulate in stromal regions but fail to penetrate tumor nests. Here, using discovery and non-overlapping internal validation cohorts of ICB-treated NSCLC patients, we show that spatial CD8+ T-cell exclusion is associated with lower objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival. To characterize the molecular programs linked to this phenotype, we integrated GeoMx spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic profiling, TCR-probe expression analysis, multiplex immunohistofluorescence, and single-cell spatial neighborhood analyses. Compared with infiltrated tumors, immune-excluded tumors showed reduced expression of genes encoding antigen-presentation machinery in the tumor compartment, including HLA class I genes and TAP1, with an altered relationship between IFN-γ-associated transcriptional signals and expression of antigen-presentation machinery. At the stromal level, excluded tumors were enriched for myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast programs and peri-epithelial collagen-rich architecture, whereas infiltrated tumors displayed immune-supportive stromal signatures. CD8-enriched regions from excluded tumors showed reduced metabolic activation and lower TCR-probe expression diversity, without a marked increase in canonical exhaustion markers. These findings provide an integrated, compartment-resolved description of tumor-intrinsic and stromal features associated with immune exclusion in NSCLC and support further evaluation of spatial immune contexture as a complementary biomarker in ICB-treated patients.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death, characterized by high mortality rates, tumor adaptation and heterogeneity, and immune evasion mechanisms. Despite recent advancements in chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery, survival rates for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remain low, signifying the need for new strategies and innovative treatments. This review explores the combinatorial potential of immunotherapy with direct targeting of tumor growth to address the multifaceted challenges of NSCLC. Key approaches include small-molecule inhibitors, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibition, angiogenesis inhibition, and nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems. Nanocarrier systems enable coordinated drug release and pharmacological synergy, thereby ensuring effective inhibition of pathways in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Additionally, this review addresses several resistance mechanisms in the context of specific inhibitors (e.g., EGFR and ALK inhibitors). Translational insights help bridge preclinical findings to clinical applications with an emphasis on angiogenesis inhibition and personalized approaches. Ethical considerations such as consent and preclinical safety testing are emphasized to ensure the safe development of these therapies. With the new generation of genetic engineering, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies for tumor growth, this work discusses the potential to transform lung cancer treatment.
